turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hey come on in. Sorry, this computer's still spinning. Have a seat.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): It's fine. I was stuck on the 101 forever anyway.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Accident?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Some truck. Forty minutes. And it's so muggy my AC just gave up.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Yeah yesterday my kid's soccer got canceled, rain, and today it's a swamp. You waiting on anyone or you drove yourself?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Drove myself. My granddaughter's with her mom. She's three. Drew a purple T rex all over the fridge and wouldn't quit talking about it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ha. Purple T rex. Okay, chart finally loaded. What are we seeing you for?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It's nothing. I felt a little bump.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Whereabouts?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): Left breast. I was in the shower. Almost didn't bother coming, it's tiny.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sorry, a window popped over your note. Left breast, say that again?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Left breast. Little lump. I figure it's a cyst.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): When did you notice it?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm I can't tell you when it started. Maybe a week. I only really clocked it yesterday in the shower. Could be longer, I don't know.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it hurt?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Not at all. If it hurt I'd worry. It doesn't.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any nipple discharge? Blood, or clear fluid, anything?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any dimpling or redness of the skin?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Nope. Looks normal.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Medicines?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Only my thyroid pill. Uh sinthroid, seventy five, every morning. Don't even count it.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Sinthroid? You mean Synthroid, levothyroxine, 75 micrograms?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah that. Micrograms. For my thyroid. I've had it for years, it's fine.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any family history of breast cancer?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): My mom. She was fifty five. Breast cancer. I'm forty six, I'm not her.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): Fifty-five, mother, breast cancer. Let me get that in. Screen lagged. Is that right?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. That's right. She got treated. This thing is a pea. I'm not doing all that.

[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright let me feel. There's a firm mobile nodule in the upper outer left breast, about 2 centimeters, not fixed to the skin. No puckering. Nipple isn't retracted. I don't feel nodes in the left axilla. Right breast is normal.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Two centimeters. Please. It's a pea. You're hyping it up.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm just saying what I feel. Look, plenty of these are cysts. We can book a routine mammogram sometime in the next month or two and I'll see you back in three months.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): See? No big deal.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Hang on. Wrong tab. Your mom was how old again?
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Fifty five. Breast cancer. You just typed it.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. No. Scratch the three months and scratch the routine mammogram. I'm not sitting on a two centimeter lump with that history.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh for goodness sake.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thursday morning you're down for a diagnostic mammogram and an ultrasound at the breast center. No deodorant, no lotion under the arms that morning, it ruins the films.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday. That's really soon.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm also referring you urgently to the breast clinic. They have you Friday. If the mammogram and the ultrasound come back borderline, then we do a biopsy. Only if.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): A biopsy. Wonderful.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): My impression, it's probably a cyst or a fibroadenoma, but I can't rule cancer out. Come back and see me in two weeks and we'll go through the results.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Two weeks. I still think you're overdoing it.

spec.situation: Woman in her forties who found a painless lump in the left breast in the shower; no nipple discharge; mother had breast cancer at fifty-five; examination described; urgent clinic referral.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
tangent_small_talk: a long tangent or small talk (traffic, cricket, the weather, a grandchild) that holds NO clinical content; nothing from it is extracted.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Doctor changed the initial plan: first mentioned a routine mammogram in the next month or two with follow-up in three months, then explicitly canceled that plan after confirming the mother's breast cancer at age 55 ('Scratch the three months and scratch the routine mammogram').
